==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|chaf}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċeaf}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kaf}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|caff}}, {{cog|stq|Sääf}}, {{cog|fy|tsjêf}}, {{cog|nl|kaf}}, {{cog|nds-de|Kaff}}, regional {{cog|de|Kaff}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/t͡ʃæf/|/t͡ʃɑːf/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-chaff.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/t͡ʃæf/|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|æf|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# The [[inedible]] parts of a [[grain]]-producing plant.
#: {{cot|en|bran}}
#: {{ux|en|To separate out the '''chaff''', early cultures tossed baskets of grain into the air and let the wind blow away the lighter '''chaff'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|The Cock and the Fox
|passage=So take the corn and leave the '''chaff''' behind.}}
# [[straw|Straw]] or [[hay]] cut up fine for the food of cattle.
#* {{quote-book|en|title=The Horse|author=w:William Youatt|year=1831|page=130|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/horseyou00youa/page/130/mode/1up|passage=By adding '''chaff''' to his corn, the horse must take more time to eat it, and time is given for the commencement of digestion, before fermentation can occur. In this way '''chaff''' is very useful, especially after long fasts.}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} Any excess or unwanted material, resource, or person; anything [[worthless]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=II|scene=ix|passage=the '''chaff''' and ruin of the times}}
# Light jesting talk; [[banter]]; [[raillery]].
#* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis||passage=As for Huxter, perfectly at good-humour with himself, and the world, it never entered his mind that he could be disagreeable to anybody; and the little dispute, or “'''chaff''',” as he styled it, of Vauxhall, was a trifle which he did not in the least regard.|51}}
#* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=It was the '''chaff''' of the College at the time, but I could not help it.}}
# {{lb|en|military}} Loose material, e.g. small strips of aluminum foil dropped from [[aircraft]], intended to [[interfere]] with [[radar]] [[detection]].
#: {{synonyms|en|window}}
#: {{hyponyms|en|rope}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To use light, idle language by way of fun or ridicule; to [[banter]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make fun of; to turn into ridicule by addressing in ironical or bantering language.
#: {{syn|en|quiz}}
#* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis||passage=We were talking about it at mess, yesterday, and '''chaffing''' Derby Oaks—until he was as mad as a hatter.|10}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1851|year_published=1861|author=w:Henry Mayhew
|title=w:London Labour and the London Poor
|passage=I’ve fallen asleep on my step as the ’bus was going on, and almost fallen off. I have often to put up with insolence from vulgar fellows, who think it fun to '''chaff''' a cad, as they call it.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1889|year_published=1899|author={{w|Rudyard Kipling}}|title={{w|Under the Deodars}}|chapter=Only A Subaltern|location=Boston|publisher=The Greenock Press|page=148|text=Bobby Wick stormed through the tents of his Company, rallying, rebuking, mildly, as is consistent with the Regulations, '''chaffing''' the faint-hearted[.]}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut up (straw or hay) for use as cattle feed.
